solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Congregation is to collapse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a church's flock of worshippers
second meaning: to give way or fail, as a business does

explanation.surface: A dwindling church whose worshippers are about to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The fold is the sheep pen, and by extension the Christian flock gathered in a church; a business that folds collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor's flock is called the fold, and a failing company is said to fold when it shuts down.

clue.text: Check progress of translation of "wolf": "loup"

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so the letters given are rendered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it is French for the same animal

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether the French word for wolf is a good rendering of the English one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites an actual translation, but loup really is the French word, so the clue looks complete; the translating is done to the letters instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow up a matter is to pursue it later and see how things have developed since.

clue.text: Television screening priestly tribe

indicators.note: a screen conceals what is behind it, so the word sits concealed inside the text

parts.note: the third to sixth letters

explanation.surface: A TV channel broadcasting a documentary about an ancient religious caste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' reads as showing a programme, but here it means hiding something within.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the descendants of Levi formed the tribe from which Israel's priests and temple servants came.

clue.text: Caught exactly what is required in authentic poetry reading

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one part goes within another

parts.note: authentic means genuine
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
as in 'that's just it', the very thing wanted

explanation.surface: A performance of verse that captures precisely what the audience needed.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus IT goes inside REAL. 'Caught' looks like a verb about the reading capturing something, but it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a public performance, often of music but also of verse spoken aloud to listeners.

clue.text: Badly defeated, sent on a course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: beaten heavily, put to flight
second meaning: directed along a particular path

explanation.surface: A team thrashed and then packed off along some route.
explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated words share the same spelling: one from a rout in battle, the other from a route on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: An army routed has been crushed and scattered; a parcel routed has been dispatched along a set path.

clue.text: Intense nervousness of dog reportedly shows unsteadiness

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed
wobbles are unsteady movements

explanation.surface: An anxious dog trembling on its legs.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the dog is said, not spelt: the breed's sound gives the first part, and the second is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The collywobbles is an informal term for a fit of nerves or a queasy anxious stomach.

clue.text: Cross party-goers stuck in centre of Ostend

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so one part sits within another
the centre is the middle part, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two of six letters
ravers are people who go to wild parties

explanation.surface: Angry clubbers stranded in the middle of a Belgian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, describing the party-goers, but it is a verb meaning to go across. RAVERS sits between the T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or over an area from one side to the other.

clue.text: By no means the first to survive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: final, coming at the end
second meaning: to endure, keep going

explanation.surface: Someone who was far from the first to come through an ordeal alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of first is final; and something that lasts endures over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means at the very end of a sequence, and the verb means to continue or hold out.

clue.text: Relative is horrible — want out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in order, so the letters are put into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful family member, and the speaker wishes to be rid of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'want out' sound like a wish to escape; 'out' is the signal working on both words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother-in-law is a relation by marriage, a spouse's brother or a sibling's husband.

clue.text: Some northerners sip unrivalled cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture of ingredients, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People in the north of England drinking a cocktail beyond compare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' looks like the drink being sipped, but it is the signal working on the words before it. Liverpool is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpudlians are natives of Liverpool, one group among the many peoples of northern England.

clue.text: In cup match, time is a minute short

indicators.note: being short means lacking something, so a letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
m is the standard abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A football cup game in which the clock runs a minute under the full time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a referee's timing error; TIME loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: In British knockout competitions such as the FA Cup, each fixture between two teams is called a tie.

clue.text: Anger fellow rather inhibits

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold something in, so the word is held within the text

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and the first five of the second

explanation.surface: A man who is somewhat restrained in showing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' could be a verb, as in to anger a fellow, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is an old and literary word for extreme rage or fury.

clue.text: Movement of Timor Sea is what creates mist

indicators.note: movement means shifting about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The swell of a tropical sea throwing spray into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Timor Sea lies between Timor and Australia, so the surface sounds like ocean science about sea spray.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device, such as a perfume spray, that turns liquid into a fine spray of droplets.

clue.text: A little condensation that's right under your nose?

definitions.text: A little condensation that's right under your nose?

parts.note: surface reading: a small bead of moisture formed from vapour, as on grass in the morning
setter's reading: a drip hanging at the tip of a nose on a cold day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Right under your nose' is an idiom for something obvious, but here it is literal: the droplet hangs from the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning bead of moisture on a leaf has a jocular second sense as a drip on a runny nose.

clue.text: Titles always found in poetry filling contents of books

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one part goes within another

parts.note: pages are what a book is made of
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Book titles which always turn up stuffed with verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titles' suggests the names of books, which the surface encourages, but it means ranks of nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A peerage is the rank of a duke, earl, baron and so on, conferring a noble title.

clue.text: What's required by computer professional? Good memory

parts.note: short for professional
standard abbreviation for good
random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A job advert asking what an IT specialist needs, answered with a good memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark seems to end the definition at 'computer professional'; in fact 'professional' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer cannot run without software instructions, and in computing the spelling of that word drops the final letters.

clue.text: Large numbers of minute beasts

parts.note: standard abbreviation for minute
asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: Swarms of tiny creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like the adjective for tiny, but it is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Masses of something means a great quantity or crowd of it.

clue.text: Cockney's to take a breath for a long note

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker turns a th sound into v, so the word is spelt as that accent says it

parts.note: breathe said with a Cockney v for th

explanation.surface: A singer told when to breathe so they can hold a sustained note.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, in which th is often said as v or f.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note lasting twice as long as a semibreve, the longest in common use.

clue.text: Priest's vestment, a pound

parts.note: taken as written
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A clerical robe on sale for a quid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests money, but the abbreviation needed is the weight, from Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is the long white linen robe worn by clergy celebrating the Eucharist.

clue.text: Crisis involving Eden upset God

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue that turns the letters bottom to top

parts.note: the 1956 Suez Crisis, under Prime Minister Anthony Eden

explanation.surface: A disaster in the Garden of Eden that angered the Almighty.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden here is not the biblical garden but Anthony Eden, the British prime minister brought down by the 1956 Suez Crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the king of the gods in Greek mythology, ruler of Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Uproar beginning to enliven feast

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A noisy start that livens up a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feast' reads as a noun, a banquet, but it is the verb, to eat well.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast is to eat heartily, and to dine is to eat a meal, especially a grand one.

clue.text: What hearing aid can offer for light music

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: making it effortless to hear
second meaning: a genre of gentle, undemanding popular music

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the genre's name: a hearing aid really does make hearing easier.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy listening is the name for mellow, melodic popular music played in lounges and lifts.

clue.text: Son goes very slowly and writes illegibly

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for son
to crawl is to move at a snail's pace

explanation.surface: A boy who dawdles and has messy handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to write hastily and carelessly so the result is hard to read.

clue.text: Sounds from cat in desirable street

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cat's soft cries
second meaning: a row of former stables converted into sought-after homes

explanation.surface: A cat crying out in a smart residential road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a mews is a lane of old stables behind grand houses, now converted into expensive cottages.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat mews when it makes small high cries, and mews houses in London are prized addresses.
